entries.title: Genesis 28:2
segments: Parents who rightly regard the good of their children, for this life or the future, or that of their descendants, will especially desire that they be connected with pious companions.

entries.title: Genesis 28:4
segments: The blessing of Abraham; that which was promised to him.

entries.title: Genesis 28:9
segments: Unto Ishmael; the family of Ishmael, he being dead.

When persons undertake to cure or to lessen one evil by the commission of another, they must expect to be disappointed.  The further they go in transgression the greater the mischief, and the greater the danger of utter ruin.

entries.title: Genesis 28:11
segments: If mem, through their own fault, are deprived of numerous blessings, and are left desolate and alone, they sometimes, during the silence and darkness of night, or in scenes of solitude, gloom, and peril, reflect on their condition, and are brought into such a state of mind as to be prepared, through grace, for new and glorious manifestations of divine favor.

entries.title: Genesis 28:16
segments: God is much nearer to us than we are apt to imagine.  Wherever we go, and whatever we do, we are surrounded continually with his presence. He keeps the breath in our nostrils, the blood flowing in our veins, and it is in him that we live, move, and have existence.

entries.title: Genesis 28:17
segments:
The house of God; the place where God revealed himself in a special way. 
 
  The gate of heaven; in allusion to the ladder reaching to heaven, by which the angels descended from heaven and returned, as through the gate of a city.

entries.title: Genesis 28:18
segments: Poured oil upon the top of it; in token of its being consecrated to God as a memorial of what there took place.

entries.title: Genesis 28:19
segments:
Beth-el; meaning the house of God.  It was about ten miles north of Jerusalem. 
 
  That city; a city that stood near this place.

entries.title: Genesis 28:22
segments:
God's house; a place where I will publicly acknowledge and adore him. 
 
  Give the tenth; devote a tenth part of what he should have to acts of piety and mercy. 
 
Whenever we receive special favors, we should feel under special obligations to acknowledge and adore God, the author and finisher of all good; and should, without delay, consecrate ourselves and all that we have to his service.
